text.p: DAOU Systems Inc Wednesday said it will acquire Integrex Systems Corp, a technology and telecommunications focused on health care markets, in exchange for 700,000 common shares valued at $11.4 million.
The deal will be accounted for as a pooling of interests. Completion is expected within two days, and Integrex will become a wholly owned unit of DAOU.
In a statement, DAOU said it believes the merger will accrete to earnings by 1997's third quarter, but further financial expectations were undisclosed. DAOU's shares were up 1-1/2 to 20-1/2.
The move will bolster DAOU's presence in the eastern United States and give it added expertise in voice and video networks that are increasingly being used by health groups.

"We view this as an outstanding opportunity for our clients," said Daniel Daou, president of DAOU Systems. "Our organizations are very much alike in technical expertise, health care market focus and core services.
The two, however, differ in that DAOU provides primarily data networks, while Integrex specializes in voice and video networks.

"We believe that the health care market is positioned to begin adopting asynchronous transfer mode technology, and we intend to be there to offer a full complement of voice, video and data services," he said.
Following the merger Kirby Farrell, chief executive officer of Integrex, will serve as vice president in charge of DAOU's telecommunications consulting services group. No layoffs are expected.

The combined company will operate six regional offices from its San Diego headquarters, employ a staff of more than 200 and will have provided services to more than 400 health care organizations throughout the United States.
